claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.

In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a newer execution can overtake an older execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it starts (it does not protect an execution until it is actually running).

In a CodePipeline pipeline using SUPERSEDED mode whose CodeBuild stage runs `pulumi up`, a queued execution waiting behind a busy stage can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment rather than colliding with one in progress.
Setting the AWS CodePipeline execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue so each runs in turn rather than being superseded by a later execution.
AWS CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (`pipelineType` V2).
The AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can set `executionMode` and `pipelineType` for a CodePipeline pipeline.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.

The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource is described later on the same page (in the 'Manage the pipeline with Pulumi' section) and its registry page exists at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that a deployment job targets, which can prevent concurrent runs from reaching the same stack.
In Azure DevOps, the exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is set on the stage that references the environment with the exclusive lock check.
The Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` setting defaults to `runLatest`.
Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` accepts the values `sequential` and `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and an older run waiting behind it is passed over rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, Azure Pipelines runs every queued stage against the lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, one at a time in order (the same way `sequential` lock behavior does).
The `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource in the Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The link /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ exists in the Pulumi Registry.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists and describes update conflicts.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts inputs `command: up`, `stack`, and `args`.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, a `deployment` job with `environment` and `strategy: runOnce: deploy: steps` is a valid structure.
When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent builds target the same stack, the second build's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict error.
The docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists and describes update conflicts.
TeamCity's default behavior is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" located under the configuration's General Settings.
The TeamCity option "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" defaults to 0, meaning unlimited.
Setting TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" to 1 causes a second build to be queued behind the first and run only after the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud has a per-stack lease that gives one-at-a-time update behavior.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by a deployment job, with `lockBehavior: sequential` on the stage, serializes deployments.
Azure Pipelines YAML stages support a `lockBehavior` property, and `sequential` is a valid value that queues runs against an exclusive lock check.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section anchored '#serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
The default AWS CodePipeline execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
AWS CodePipeline pipeline execution mode has a value named `QUEUED`.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section anchored '#serialize-pipeline-executions'.
In TeamCity, setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 on the build configuration serializes deployments.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds'.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section anchored '#limit-concurrent-builds'.
